story.text: The admission ceremony has a second tongue: the Trust Over IP *Trust Task* envelope — a small signed JSON document (`id · type · payload · issuer · recipient · threadId · proof`) that carries one finite unit of verifiable work. [[The Ceremony]] emits six of them: apply, respond, approve, issue, revoke, status.

The translation preserved the laws, not just the shapes. [[The Two Gates]] became a schema constraint (exactly two gate results, of two distinct kinds, or no credential); [[The Verdict Lexicon]] a closed three-value enum; the credential inside the issue envelope is the bilateral pair, and the agent's counter-signature travels back on the wire, signed with its own real key.

Evidence never floats: every gate result names the audit-event hash that records it, and the whole thing is re-proven on each run — a zero-dependency auditor over the vendored schemas, and the end-to-end ceremony re-spoken as envelopes with byte-exact hash parity. A relying party needs none of our screens: the status read is a signed document anything can verify. See [[The Evidence]].
A spoken standard invites a second speaker — and the family's own promotion bar demands one. It exists: [[The Second Implementation]].
